religions.title: Christianity
religions.note: Those who confess Jesus as Lord and hold the Bible as Scripture: the common ground is wide, and the conversation is over what the Bible says.

religions.title: Judaism
religions.note: Those who hold the Law and the Prophets: begin from the Hebrew Scriptures and the promises.

religions.title: Islam
religions.note: Those who honour Jesus as a prophet and the Messiah, but not as the Son of God who died and rose: begin from the one God and the history of the cross.

religions.title: Bahá'í Faith
religions.note: Those who hold Bahá'u'llah the latest of God's messengers, after Moses, Jesus and Muhammad: begin from the Scripture they honour, and its warning against later prophets.

religions.title: Hinduism
religions.note: Many traditions, most holding rebirth and karma and many forms of the divine: begin from the Creator and the one life.

religions.title: Sikhism
religions.note: One God, the Creator, known by the Name and the Gurus' teaching: begin from the one Creator and the grace of God.

religions.title: Buddhism
religions.note: A path to end suffering, without a Creator: begin from suffering, its cause, and the resurrection that ends it.

religions.title: No religion
religions.note: Those who hold no faith: begin from history and the world itself, not from the Bible's authority.

audiences.title: Catholics
audiences.note: Catholic teaching holds the Trinity, an immortal soul judged at death to heaven, purgatory or hell, the baptism of infants, tradition and the Pope's teaching office beside Scripture, and the intercession of Mary and the saints. Begin from the creeds' own words, "the resurrection of the body": if the dead are conscious already, why is it needed?

audiences.title: Eastern Orthodox
audiences.note: Orthodox Christians hold the Trinity as the councils defined it, holy tradition beside Scripture, the veneration of icons, the intercession of the Mother of God and the saints, and the baptism of infants by threefold immersion. Begin from the resurrection, which the Orthodox hold at the centre of their faith, and from what the apostles themselves wrote.

audiences.title: Coptic, Ethiopian, Armenian and Syriac Orthodox
audiences.note: The Oriental Orthodox churches hold the Trinity and that Christ has one nature, at once divine and human; holy tradition and the liturgy beside Scripture, the Ethiopian canon wider still, with Enoch and Jubilees; the intercession of Mary and the saints, icons, fasting, and the baptism of infants. Begin from the apostles' writings, which they read in the oldest tongues, and from the resurrection they keep at the heart of their year.

audiences.title: Anglicans and Episcopalians
audiences.note: Anglicans hold the creeds and the Trinity, two sacraments, the baptism of infants, bishops, priests and deacons, and a soul that goes to God at death; they range from evangelical to Anglo-Catholic and liberal. Their own Articles say Scripture "containeth all things necessary to salvation", and read the Apocrypha "for example of life" but not for doctrine: begin there, and test each teaching by the Scripture they confess suffices.

audiences.title: Lutherans
audiences.note: Lutherans hold Scripture alone and salvation by grace through faith alone, the Trinity, baptism as a means of grace given to infants, and the body and blood of Christ truly present in, with and under the bread and wine. Begin from Luther's own ground, Scripture over councils and popes, and carry it through to the soul, the supper and baptism.

audiences.title: Reformed and Presbyterians
audiences.note: Reformed churches hold Scripture alone, God's sovereign choice of those he will save and their perseverance to the end, the Trinity, the baptism of believers' infants as a sign of the covenant, and worship without images. Begin from the covenant with Abraham, which they rightly set at the centre, and ask what it promised: the land, for ever, at the resurrection.

audiences.title: Methodists and Wesleyans
audiences.note: Methodists hold that grace is offered to all and may be refused, that a believer can fall away, and that God calls his people to holiness; they hold the Trinity, the baptism of infants, and going to God at death. Begin from the common ground on free grace and holy living, then from the hope Wesley's hymns still sing, the resurrection at Christ's coming.

audiences.title: Baptists
audiences.note: Baptists hold Scripture alone, the baptism of believers by immersion, the bread and wine as a memorial, the priesthood of all believers and the self-government of each congregation; most hold the Trinity, going to heaven at death and eternal punishment, many that the saved cannot be lost, and many a rapture before the tribulation. Begin from the large common ground on baptism and the supper, then ask why baptism was preached as for the remission of sins.

audiences.title: Mennonites, Amish and Anabaptists
audiences.note: Anabaptists hold the baptism of believers only, the bread and wine as a memorial, a church separate from the world and its powers, and refusal to bear arms or swear oaths; they hold the Trinity and going to God at death. They share more than most with the brethren's own way of life: begin from that common ground, and from the kingdom Christ will set up, for which his people wait as strangers here.

audiences.title: Evangelicals
audiences.note: Evangelicals hold the Bible's authority, the Trinity, salvation by faith, going to heaven at death and eternal punishment in hell. The shared regard for Scripture is the way in: ask what a passage says before what it is taken to mean.

audiences.title: Pentecostals and charismatics
audiences.note: Pentecostals hold the Trinity, the holy spirit as a person giving gifts today, and spiritual warfare against the devil and demons. Begin from what the spirit is in Scripture, God's power, and from Jesus' own healings.

audiences.title: Oneness Pentecostals
audiences.note: Oneness Pentecostals hold that God is one and not three persons, but that Jesus is himself the Father, the Son and the spirit; they baptise by immersion in the name of Jesus for the remission of sins, and hold speaking in tongues the sign of receiving the spirit. Begin from the large common ground, one God and baptism into the name of Jesus, then from the Son praying to his Father.

audiences.title: Churches of Christ and Restorationists
audiences.note: Churches of Christ seek to restore the first-century church without creeds: believers baptised by immersion for the remission of sins, the bread and wine every first day of the week, elders over each congregation, and the spirit gifts ended with the apostles. Most hold the Trinity, the soul going to God at death and eternal punishment. Begin from the plea they share, the Bible alone, and carry it through to the hope of Israel and the nature of man.

audiences.title: Seventh-day Adventists
audiences.note: Adventists hold that the dead sleep until the resurrection, that the wicked are destroyed rather than tormented, and that Christ will return in person, and they baptise by immersion. They hold the Trinity, a personal devil, a thousand years in heaven before the earth is made new, and the seventh-day sabbath, and count Ellen White's writings a continuing source of truth. Begin from the common ground on death.

audiences.title: Jehovah's Witnesses
audiences.note: Witnesses hold that God is one and not a Trinity, that the soul dies, that hell is the grave, and that the kingdom will be on the earth. They hold that Jesus existed before his birth as Michael the archangel, that the devil is a fallen angel, that Christ's presence began invisibly in 1914, and that 144,000 reign in heaven. Begin from the large common ground.

audiences.title: Latter-day Saints
audiences.note: Latter-day Saints hold that the Father and the Son are separate beings, that all people lived as spirits before birth, and that the Book of Mormon and later revelations are Scripture beside the Bible, which they hold to be true as far as it is translated correctly; they look for Christ's return to reign on the earth and baptise by immersion. Begin from the Bible's account of man made from the dust.

audiences.title: Christian Scientists
audiences.note: Christian Science, from Mary Baker Eddy's Science and Health, holds that God is Mind and all that is real is spiritual, so that matter, sickness, sin and death are illusions to be healed by right understanding; Jesus is the man who showed the Christ, not God, and his blood did not atone. Begin from the Bible's own account of sin, pain and death as real, and of a Saviour who truly died and rose.

audiences.title: Quakers (Friends)
audiences.note: Friends hold that the inner light of Christ is in every person and guides them directly; they keep no outward baptism or supper, no clergy, and plain, silent worship, and are known for peace and integrity. Many today are liberal or universalist. Begin from the common ground of worship without priests or images, then ask where the light is to be tested: "To the law and to the testimony."

audiences.title: Liberal and progressive Christians
audiences.note: Liberal Christians hold the Bible a human record of faith, its miracles and authorship open to doubt, evolution settled, and Jesus' teaching on love its heart; many hold that all will be saved, and many have already set aside hell and a personal devil. Begin from that common ground, then from the evidence: the records, fulfilled prophecy, and the empty tomb.

audiences.title: Biblical Unitarians
audiences.note: Biblical Unitarians, among them the Church of God of the Abrahamic Faith, hold that God is one, the Father, that Jesus is his Son who began at his birth, and that the holy spirit is God's power; many hold the soul mortal, the dead asleep and the kingdom on the earth. The common ground is very wide: begin from it, and raise the adversary and the spirit gifts, where some differ.

audiences.title: Unitarian Universalists
audiences.note: Unitarian Universalists grew from churches that held God one and all to be saved, and now hold no creed: members may be Christian, theist, humanist or Buddhist, and seek truth by reason and conscience. Begin from the history they honour, the one God their founders found in Scripture, then from the evidence that Jesus rose.

audiences.title: Messianic Jews and Hebrew Roots
audiences.note: Messianic Jews confess Jesus, Yeshua, the Messiah of Israel while keeping the sabbath, the feasts and much of the law; Hebrew Roots believers, many of them Gentiles, seek the same. Most hold the Trinity and going to heaven at death. Begin from the large common ground in the promises to Israel, then from the new covenant that Jeremiah foretold.

audiences.title: Orthodox and traditional Jews
audiences.note: Orthodox Judaism holds that God is one, the Torah written and oral, the resurrection of the dead, and a Messiah of David's line who will gather Israel and reign on the earth; it rejects Jesus, often because Christians call him God. Begin from the Shema and the promises: Jesus fulfils them without being a second God.

audiences.title: Reform and secular Jews
audiences.note: Reform and secular Jews hold Jewish identity and ethics, often without a personal Messiah, a resurrection of the dead, or the Torah as given by God word for word. Begin from history: Israel's scattering and return, and the evidence that Jesus rose.

audiences.title: Sunni and Shia Muslims
audiences.note: Islam holds that God is one, and that Jesus was a prophet and the Messiah, born of a virgin, but not the Son of God, and that he was not crucified but taken up, and will return before the end. It holds the Qur'an God's final word, the earlier Scriptures changed, and a man judged by his deeds. Begin from the one God, and from the evidence that Jesus died and rose.

audiences.title: Ahmadi Muslims
audiences.note: Ahmadis hold that Jesus was put on the cross but taken down alive, recovered, and died in old age in Kashmir, and that his promised return was fulfilled in Mirza Ghulam Ahmad. Begin from the common ground that he was crucified, then from the evidence that he died there and rose.

audiences.title: Bahá'ís
audiences.note: Bahá'ís hold one God revealed in turn by messengers, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, Muhammad, the Báb and Bahá'u'llah, whose coming in 1844 and after they count Christ's promised return and the Comforter he spoke of; they hold the unity of all religions, an immortal soul that grows after death, and the resurrection as spiritual. Begin from the one God and from what Jesus said of his own return.

audiences.title: Devotional Hindus
audiences.note: Vaishnavas, Shaivas and Hare Krishnas worship a personal Lord, Vishnu, Krishna or Shiva, who comes down in avatars; they hold rebirth and karma, worship before images, and may count Jesus a holy man or an avatar among many. Begin from the one Creator, and from the one life Scripture gives.

audiences.title: Advaita Hindus and yoga
audiences.note: Advaita holds that only Brahman is real, that the self is one with it, that the world and its suffering are illusion, and that liberation is knowing this and escaping rebirth; much Western yoga and meditation teaching comes from it. Begin from the world as made and real, and from sin and death as real.

audiences.title: Sikhs
audiences.note: Sikhs hold one God, the Creator, formless and worshipped without images, known by meditating on the Name; the ten Gurus and the Guru Granth Sahib as the Word; rebirth and karma, ended by God's grace; and that God may be reached by many paths. Begin from the one Creator and from grace.

audiences.title: Buddhists
audiences.note: Buddhists, Theravada and Mahayana, follow the Buddha's path to end suffering, which they trace to craving; they hold rebirth and karma without a Creator or an enduring self, and seek nirvana. Begin from suffering, which both take seriously, and from the denial of an immortal soul, which both share.

audiences.title: Sceptics and atheists
audiences.note: Begin from history and reason, not from the Bible's authority. Common ground first: Jesus lived and was crucified, man is mortal, and no one is tormented for ever. Then show that the Bible's faith rests on evidence and that miracles are not incredible if there is a God; then the empty tomb, the witnesses and the records, prophecy fulfilled and the world as made. Answer the hard passages on morals when they are raised.

audiences.title: Agnostics and the spiritual but not religious
audiences.note: Agnostics are unsure whether God can be known; the spiritual but not religious often hold that every path leads to the same place and that the self has a spark of the divine. Begin from what can be known: the world as made, and the evidence that Jesus rose.

audiences.title: Former believers
audiences.note: Those who left a church, often over hell, suffering, the Bible's hard passages or its apparent contradictions. Many rejected what the Bible does not teach: begin by setting its plain teaching apart from the creeds they left, then answer the hard passages, then the evidence that Jesus rose.

entries.subject: creation
entries.title: The world was made, and declares its Maker
entries.summary: The world had a beginning, and what begins has a cause. "Every house is builded by some man; but he that built all things is God." The heavens declare his glory, and his eternal power and Godhead are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, so that those who deny him are without excuse. The earth was formed to be inhabited, and life is ordered for it. The Bible's God is not a force within the world but its Maker, distinct from what he made.

points.claim: The world had a beginning; God was before it.
What is made shows a maker, as a house shows a builder.
The earth was formed to be inhabited, and its life is kept by him.
The Creator is distinct from what he made; worshipping the creature instead of him is the root of idolatry.

objections.objection: Science has explained the world without God.
objections.answer: Science describes how the world works; it cannot say why there is a world at all, or why it is ordered so that it can be understood. That it began, and is fitted for life, is what a Creator would lead us to expect.

objections.objection: Who made God?
objections.answer: What begins needs a cause; God did not begin. He is from everlasting to everlasting.

objections.objection: All is God, and the self is God, though it has forgotten.
objections.answer: Scripture keeps the Creator and his creature apart: "I am God, and not man." Man is dust, made and mortal, and those who changed the glory of the Creator into the likeness of the creature are the ones Paul calls fools.

entries.subject: creation
entries.title: God made the world in six days, a few thousand years ago
entries.summary: Each day of Genesis 1 is numbered and bounded by an evening and a morning, and the fourth commandment rests the week on them: "in six days Yahweh made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day." The genealogies run unbroken from Adam to Abraham, giving their years, and Luke runs them on to Jesus. Jesus said man was made male and female "from the beginning of the creation", not at the end of ages. Death came into the world by Adam's sin, so there were no ages of death before him. The earth is thousands of years old, not billions.

points.claim: Each day is numbered and bounded by an evening and a morning.
The fourth commandment rests man's week on God's: six days of work, and the seventh a rest.
The genealogies run from Adam to Abraham with their years, and Luke runs them on to Jesus; Enoch was the seventh from Adam.
Man was made male and female from the beginning of the creation, not at the end of long ages.
God made all very good; death entered by Adam's sin.

objections.objection: With the Lord a day is as a thousand years.
objections.answer: Peter speaks of God's patience in delaying the promised day, not of the length of the days of Genesis; he says also that a thousand years are as one day. The commandment counts the days of creation as man's days of work.

objections.objection: Ages may lie between Genesis 1:1 and 1:2.
objections.answer: In six days Yahweh made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is: the heaven and earth of verse 1 are within the six days, not before them.

objections.objection: Science has measured the earth at four and a half billion years.
objections.answer: No one measured the past; the dates rest on what was assumed of it: how much there was to begin with, and that rates never changed across ages no one saw. God asks Job where he was when the earth's foundations were laid. The one witness who was there has said when.

objections.objection: Genesis is poetry, not history.
objections.answer: Genesis is told as history, with genealogies, ages and places. Jesus and Paul took Adam and Eve as the first man and woman, and Paul rests the gospel on it: as in Adam all die, so in Christ shall all be made alive.

entries.subject: creation
entries.title: Life was made after its kind, not evolved from one ancestor
entries.summary: Genesis says ten times that God made living things "after their kind", and Paul that all flesh is not the same flesh. Adam was formed from the dust and Eve from his side, not from an animal ancestor. What is seen is variation within kinds, as in Jacob's flocks and every breed of dog, not one kind becoming another. Darwin owned that the missing transitional forms were the gravest objection to his theory, and that the sudden appearance of whole groups in the lowest fossil-bearing rocks was graver still; the major groups of animals still appear there suddenly. Evolution needs ages of death before man, which Scripture says came by sin.

points.claim: God made the plants, fish, birds and beasts each after its kind.
All flesh is not the same flesh: of men, of beasts, of fish and of birds.
Adam was formed from the dust and Eve from his side; Luke ends Jesus' genealogy with "Adam, which was the son of God."
What is seen is variation within a kind, as in Jacob's flocks, not one kind becoming another.

Darwin owned that the missing transitional forms were the gravest objection to his theory, laid it to the imperfection of the fossil record, and had no answer for the sudden appearance of whole groups in the lowest fossil-bearing rocks. The major groups of animals still appear there suddenly, fully formed.

sources.quote: Firstly, why, if species have descended from other species by insensibly fine gradations, do we not everywhere see innumerable transitional forms? Why is not all nature in confusion instead of the species being, as we see them, well defined?
To the question why we do not find records of these vast primordial periods, I can give no satisfactory answer.

points.claim: Life is fearfully and wonderfully made: its order is the work of a Mind, as a house shows a builder.

objections.objection: Evolution is proven science.
objections.answer: Change within a kind is seen and is not in dispute. That all life descended from a single cell is an inference about a past no one observed, and the fossils do not show the fine gradations it requires.

objections.objection: Shared DNA shows common ancestry.
objections.answer: Likeness shows a common Maker as well as a common ancestor: one builder uses the same plans for many houses. Creatures made of one dust, for one world, are alike where they must be.

objections.objection: God could have used evolution.
objections.answer: Then ages of death, struggle and suffering before Adam are what God called very good, and death did not come by sin. But Paul's gospel rests on a first man by whom death came, as by the second comes the resurrection.

entries.subject: creation
entries.title: The flood covered the whole earth
entries.summary: The waters prevailed over all the high hills under the whole heaven, and every living thing on the land died except those in the ark. A local flood needed no ark a hundred and twenty years in building, and would break God's promise never again to destroy the earth by a flood, for local floods come every year. Jesus and Peter speak of the flood as history and a pattern of judgement to come. A flood over the whole earth for a year would lay down rock in layers and bury creatures by the billion: much of what is read as ages is the record of that judgement.

points.claim: The waters covered all the high hills under the whole heaven, and all flesh on the land died.
God promised never again to destroy the earth by a flood; local floods come every year, so the flood was not local.
Jesus and Peter speak of the flood as history, and the pattern of the judgement to come.
The fountains of the great deep broke up; afterwards the mountains rose and the valleys sank, and the waters went down.

objections.objection: The rock layers took millions of years to form.
objections.answer: Slow deposition is assumed, not seen. Water moving over the whole earth for a year lays down layers quickly and buries creatures before they decay, and the fossils are a record of death on a vast scale, which Scripture lays to sin and judgement.

objections.objection: Where did the water come from, and where did it go?
objections.answer: From the fountains of the great deep as well as the windows of heaven; afterwards the mountains rose and the valleys sank to the place God founded for them.

objections.objection: Flood stories are told by many nations; Genesis borrowed one.
objections.answer: If every nation is descended from Noah's sons, many nations remembering a great flood is what should be found. Genesis gives it soberly, with dates and an ark fit to float, not as a quarrel of gods.

entries.subject: creation-science
entries.title: The ark was large enough, and built to survive the flood
entries.summary: The ark was 300 cubits long, 50 broad and 30 high: about 137 by 23 by 14 metres, with three decks and some 43,000 cubic metres of space, the room of over five hundred railway stock wagons. Noah took two of every kind of air-breathing land animal and bird, and seven of the clean, not every species: a kind can hold many species, and the sea creatures stayed in the sea. Studies count at most some 16,000 animals, most no larger than a sheep, the large ones young; they fit in under half the ark, leaving room for food and water. Its proportions, length six times its breadth, are those of modern ships, and a study of naval engineers found them close to the best for stability, strength and riding out heavy seas. It was not built to sail anywhere, only to float, and God shut them in.

points.claim: The ark was 300 by 50 by 30 cubits, about 137 by 23 by 14 metres, with three decks: some 43,000 cubic metres, the room of over five hundred railway stock wagons.
Noah took two of every kind of air-breathing land animal and bird, and seven of the clean; a kind holds many species, and the creatures of the sea stayed in it.
At most some 16,000 animals were needed, most no larger than a sheep and the large ones young; they fit in under half the ark, with room for food and water.
Its proportions, length six times breadth, are those of modern ships; naval engineers found them close to the best for stability, strength and riding heavy seas.
It was built to float, not to sail, sealed with pitch within and without, and God shut them in.

objections.objection: Millions of species could not fit on one boat.
objections.answer: Noah took kinds, not species: the dogs, wolves and foxes from one pair, as the varieties seen today come from few. Insects and sea creatures were not taken, and most animals are small.

objections.objection: Eight people could not feed and clean so many animals for a year.
objections.answer: Studies of the work (Woodmorappe, 1996), using the means farmers have long used, stored food and water fed by gravity and floors that drain, find it within the strength of eight. God, who brought the animals to the ark, kept them in it.

objections.objection: No wooden ship that large could hold together.
objections.answer: The ark did not need to be driven through the sea, only to ride it; its proportions and size are those engineers judge best for that, and Noah built it as God commanded.

objections.objection: How did the animals reach distant lands afterwards?
objections.answer: They spread from Ararat as the earth was refilled, over land since parted by the sea, as men were scattered from Babel.

entries.subject: creation-science
entries.title: Fossils were buried quickly, many through layers said to span ages
entries.summary: Upright fossil tree trunks stand through several layers of rock and coal, as at Joggins in Nova Scotia; a trunk does not stand for thousands of years waiting to be buried, so the layers around it were laid down while it stood. Fossils form only when a creature is buried before it rots or is eaten, and the rocks hold them in their billions: fish caught swallowing other fish, ichthyosaurs in the act of giving birth, jellyfish with their soft outlines, whole graveyards of bones jumbled by water. Sea creatures lie in rock on every continent and at the summit of Everest. This is the record of a sudden, watery, worldwide burial, as Genesis describes.

points.claim: Upright tree trunks pass through several layers of rock and coal, as at Joggins, Nova Scotia: the layers around them were laid down while they stood, not over ages.
A fossil forms only when a creature is buried before it rots or is eaten; fish caught mid-meal, ichthyosaurs mid-birth and soft jellyfish show burial in moments.
Fossil graveyards gather bones by the thousand, jumbled and sorted by moving water.
Sea creatures lie in rock high on every continent, even at the summit of Everest: the waters stood over the mountains.

objections.objection: The upright trees grew where they stand, one forest over another, through long ages.
objections.answer: Many have no roots in place, or are cut off from their roots, and stand in sandstone laid down by water. Their trunks did not rot through the ages the layers are said to span: they were buried quickly, and so were the layers.

objections.objection: Fossils form slowly in quiet water over long ages.
objections.answer: A carcass on the sea floor is eaten or decays within weeks. What is slow is not burial but the hardening after it; a creature preserved whole, or in mid-act, was buried at once.

entries.subject: creation-science
entries.title: The rock layers were laid down quickly, and bent while soft
entries.summary: Mount St Helens, in 1980, laid down finely layered deposits many metres thick in hours, and a mudflow in 1982 cut a canyon through them in a day: layers and canyons do not need ages. In the Grand Canyon whole series of layers are folded without cracking, as though bent while still soft, though they are said to have been laid down over hundreds of millions of years. Between many layers the contact is flat and sharp, with no sign of the erosion that millions of missing years would leave. Single layers run across whole continents, as no river or local sea lays them. This is the work of the flood, not of ages.

points.claim: At Mount St Helens finely layered deposits many metres thick were laid down in hours in 1980, and a mudflow in 1982 cut a canyon through them: layers and canyons do not need ages.
Whole series of layers in the Grand Canyon are folded without cracking, as rock bends only while soft: they were laid down and folded together, not over hundreds of millions of years.
Many layers meet in flat, sharp contacts with no erosion between them, though millions of years are said to be missing there.
Single layers run across whole continents, as only waters over the whole earth would lay them.
The fountains of the great deep broke up, and as the waters went down the mountains rose and the valleys sank.

objections.objection: Geologists see the present as the key to the past: slow processes over long ages.
objections.answer: Peter foretold that men would say all things continue as they were from the beginning, willingly ignorant that the world then perished by water. The rocks themselves show catastrophe, and geologists now grant many layers were laid down quickly.

entries.subject: creation-science
entries.title: Dinosaur bones still hold soft tissue
entries.summary: In 2005 Mary Schweitzer reported flexible, branching blood vessels, with small round structures like blood cells inside them, from the thigh bone of a Tyrannosaurus rex said to be 68 million years old. Fragments of its collagen protein were later sequenced, and soft tissue has since been found in many other dinosaur bones. Proteins and vessels break down in thousands of years, not tens of millions. The bones are not as old as they are said to be: dinosaurs were made on the sixth day with the other land animals, and were buried in the flood.

points.claim: Flexible, branching vessels, with small round structures like blood cells inside, were found in a Tyrannosaurus rex thigh bone said to be 68 million years old.
Fragments of its collagen protein were sequenced, and soft tissue has since been found in many other dinosaur bones.
Proteins and vessels break down in thousands of years, not tens of millions.
The land animals, dinosaurs among them, were made on the sixth day with man; behemoth was made with Job.

objections.objection: Iron from the blood preserved the tissue for millions of years.
objections.answer: The experiment offered for it (Schweitzer and others, 2014) kept ostrich vessels soaked in concentrated blood for two years, not tens of millions, and in a state no buried bone was in. That tissue survives at all is what a young world would lead us to expect.

objections.objection: The tissue is bacterial slime, not the animal's own.
objections.answer: The collagen sequenced matched that of animals, not of bacteria, and the vessels branch and hold cell-like structures as an animal's do.

entries.subject: creation-science
entries.title: Radiometric dates fail on rocks of known age, and radiocarbon remains where none should
entries.summary: Lava from Mount St Helens that cooled in 1986 was dated by potassium-argon at 350,000 years, and lava from New Zealand flows of the 1950s at millions of years: the method gives ages to rock whose age is known, and gives them wrongly. Different methods on the same rock disagree. Radiocarbon, which cannot last 100,000 years, is found in coal and in diamonds said to be hundreds of millions or billions of years old. Helium made by decay is still in tiny zircon crystals, though it leaks out quickly enough that billions of years would have emptied them. The dates rest on assumptions; where they can be checked, they fail.

points.claim: Lava from Mount St Helens that cooled in 1986 was dated by potassium-argon at 350,000 years: the method dates rock of known age wrongly.
The dates rest on assumptions no one could see: how much of each element there was at the start, that none came in or went out, and that the rate never changed.
Radiocarbon, which cannot last 100,000 years, is found in coal and in diamonds said to be hundreds of millions or billions of years old.

sources.loc: chapter 8, Baumgardner, 14C evidence for a recent global flood and a young earth

points.claim: Helium made by decay is still held in tiny zircon crystals, though it leaks out fast enough that billions of years would have emptied them.

sources.loc: chapter 2, Humphreys, Young helium diffusion age of zircons supports accelerated nuclear decay

objections.objection: The radiocarbon in coal and diamonds is contamination.
objections.answer: Diamond is the hardest and most closed of materials, and the amounts are above the laboratories' own background and much alike in coal from every era, as from one recent burial.

objections.objection: Different methods agree on the great ages.
objections.answer: They agree when the results are chosen to agree; discordant dates are commonly set aside as disturbed. A method that fails on rock of known age cannot be trusted on rock of unknown age.

entries.subject: creation-science
entries.title: Many natural processes limit the age of the earth
entries.summary: Short-period comets lose material at every pass of the sun and would be gone in a few hundred thousand years; to keep billions of years a store of new comets is supposed, the Oort cloud, which no one has seen. The strength of the earth's magnetic field has fallen by about a tenth since it was first measured in the 1830s. At present rates the continents would be worn to sea level many times over in the age claimed. These are limits, not dates: they tell against billions of years, and agree with the thousands Scripture gives. Arguments such as the depth of moon dust and human footprints beside dinosaur tracks at Paluxy have been set aside by creationists themselves, and are not used here.

points.claim: Short-period comets wear away at every pass of the sun and would be gone in a few hundred thousand years; the Oort cloud supposed to replace them has never been seen.
The strength of the earth's magnetic field has fallen by about a tenth since it was first measured in the 1830s.
At present rates of erosion the continents would be worn to sea level many times over in the age claimed.
The heavens and the earth wax old as a garment: the creation is running down, not building up.

objections.objection: Rates were not always as they are now.
objections.answer: That is so, and it is what creationists say of the radiometric clocks. Those who assume constant rates for the dates they accept cannot set them aside for the limits they do not.

entries.subject: creation-science
entries.title: Human genetics points to a recent first pair, and a genome running down
entries.summary: Every living person's mitochondrial DNA traces back to one woman, and every man's Y chromosome to one man, as all are of one blood, from Eve and through Noah. When the mutation rate of mitochondrial DNA was measured in real families it was far faster than had been assumed; at that rate the first mother lived about 6,000 years ago. Mankind is genetically very alike, as a young race from few people would be. Harmful mutations accumulate in every generation faster than selection can remove them: the genome is running down, as the creation was made subject to corruption, not building up.

points.claim: All mankind's mitochondrial DNA traces to one woman, and all men's Y chromosomes to one man: all are of one blood.
Measured in real families, mitochondrial DNA mutates far faster than had been assumed; at that rate the first mother lived about 6,000 years ago.
Harmful mutations accumulate in every generation faster than selection removes them: the genome is running down.
Lifespans fell after the flood from near a thousand years to seventy, as a decaying inheritance would.

objections.objection: The mitochondrial Eve of science lived about 200,000 years ago and was not the only woman alive.
objections.answer: That age rests on a rate calibrated by assumed ages of descent from apes, not on the rate measured in families. That all trace to one mother is what Scripture says: she was the mother of all living.

objections.objection: Most of our DNA is junk left over from evolution.
objections.answer: The ENCODE project (2012) reported biochemical activity across most of the genome, and functions for once-dismissed DNA are found year by year. Calling what is not yet understood junk is an argument from ignorance.

entries.subject: creation-science
entries.title: Life's information could not arise by chance
entries.summary: DNA is a code, written in four letters and read by machines that are themselves built from its instructions: the code needs the machines, and the machines need the code. A working protein is a precise sequence; Douglas Axe estimated that only about one in 10^77 sequences of a modest protein's length fold to work, more than the number of atoms in our galaxy. The simplest living cell needs hundreds of such proteins at once. Natural selection cannot help before there is life to reproduce. Codes and machines come from minds: life is fearfully and wonderfully made.

points.claim: DNA is a code read by machines built from its own instructions: each needs the other from the first.
Only about one in 10^77 protein sequences of a modest length folds to work, and the simplest cell needs hundreds at once.
Natural selection works only on things that reproduce; it cannot make the first living thing.
Codes and machines come from minds: as a house shows a builder, life shows its Maker.

objections.objection: Given enough time, anything can happen.
objections.answer: The odds exceed every trial the universe could have made, and time breaks such molecules apart in water as fast as it joins them.

objections.objection: Life began in an RNA world, with molecules that copied themselves.
objections.answer: No self-copying RNA has been found to arise by itself; those made in laboratories were designed and selected by chemists, which is the point: it takes a mind.

entries.subject: creation-science
entries.title: Life's molecules are all of one hand, as chance never makes them
entries.summary: Many molecules come in left- and right-handed forms, mirror images of each other. The amino acids in living proteins are all left-handed, and the sugars in DNA and RNA all right-handed; a few of the wrong hand spoil a protein's fold or a DNA strand. Every unguided reaction makes the two hands in equal measure: Stanley Miller's famous experiment of 1953 made amino acids, but an even mixture of both. The few natural processes that favour one hand give a small excess, not the purity life needs. One-handedness is the mark of selection by a mind.

points.claim: The amino acids in living proteins are all left-handed, and the sugars of DNA and RNA all right-handed; a few of the wrong hand spoil them.
Unguided reactions make both hands equally: Miller's experiment of 1953 made amino acids, but an even mixture of both.
One-handedness is the mark of selection by a mind.

objections.objection: Some meteorites, and polarised light, show an excess of one hand.
objections.answer: The excesses found are small, and fall far short of the complete purity life needs; and a mixture enriched by a few parts still spoils every chain built from it.

entries.subject: creation-science
entries.title: Living machines need all their parts at once
entries.summary: Darwin wrote that if any complex organ could not have been formed by numerous, successive, slight modifications, his theory would absolutely break down. The bacterial flagellum is a rotary motor of some forty kinds of protein, with a rotor, stator, drive shaft and propeller, and without any of its core parts it does not turn. The clotting of blood is a cascade in which a missing step means bleeding to death or clotting solid. A part that does nothing until the whole is built gives selection nothing to keep. Such machines were made whole.

points.claim: Darwin set the test himself: an organ that could not be formed by numerous, slight steps would overthrow his theory.

sources.quote: If it could be demonstrated that any complex organ existed, which could not possibly have been formed by numerous, successive, slight modifications, my theory would absolutely break down.

points.claim: The bacterial flagellum is a rotary motor of some forty kinds of protein; without any of its core parts it does not turn.
Blood clotting is a cascade in which a missing step means bleeding to death, or clotting solid.
A part that does nothing until the whole is built gives selection nothing to keep: the hand of Yahweh has wrought this.

objections.objection: Parts of the flagellum are found in a secretion system with another use.
objections.answer: That some of its parts serve elsewhere does not show a path of small useful steps to the whole motor, and many researchers hold the secretion system came after the flagellum, not before it.

objections.objection: This is an argument from ignorance: one day the steps will be found.
objections.answer: It is an argument from what is known: machines with interlocking parts are, in every case where we know the cause, the work of a designer.

entries.subject: creation-science
entries.title: The universe and the earth are fitted for life
entries.summary: The strengths of gravity and of the forces in the atom, and the energy of empty space, lie within narrow bounds outside which there could be no stars, no chemistry and no life; the last is set to about one part in 10^120. The earth is placed at the distance from the sun where water is liquid, and water itself is unlike almost any other substance: ice floats, so lakes and seas freeze from the top and life survives beneath. Yahweh formed the earth to be inhabited, and stretched out the heavens.

points.claim: The forces of nature lie within narrow bounds outside which there could be no stars, chemistry or life; the energy of empty space is set to about one part in 10^120.
The earth is placed where water is liquid, and ice floats, so waters freeze from the top and life survives beneath.
He formed the earth to be inhabited, and made the heavens by his word.

objections.objection: There are countless universes, and we are in one that happens to fit.
objections.answer: No other universe has been or can be observed: it is a belief held to avoid a Maker, and a machine that made universes would need explaining too.

objections.objection: If it were not fitted for life we would not be here to notice.
objections.answer: A man who survives a firing squad of a hundred marksmen cannot say it was no surprise because otherwise he would not be there to wonder: he asks why they all missed.

entries.subject: creation
entries.title: Suffering came by sin, and God will end it
entries.summary: God made the world very good; death and the curse came by sin, and the creation was made subject to vanity, in hope. Time and chance happen to all, and Jesus denied that those killed in a disaster were worse sinners than others. God tempts no one to evil, and trial borne in faith works patience and hope. He has appointed a day when there shall be no more death, neither sorrow nor crying, and he raises the dead: no suffering is final.

points.claim: The world was very good; death and the curse came by sin.
The creation was made subject to vanity, in hope of deliverance.
Time and chance happen to all; disaster is not a measure of guilt.
God tempts no one to evil; trial borne in faith brings patience and hope.
He will end death and sorrow, and raise the dead.

objections.objection: A good and almighty God would end all suffering now.
objections.answer: He will, and has fixed the day; he waits because he is longsuffering, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

objections.objection: Suffering shows there is no God.
objections.answer: To call the world unjust is to measure it by a justice above it. The Bible names the cause, sin and death, and the remedy, which Jesus showed in his healings and in his own resurrection.

entries.subject: faith
entries.title: Faith rests on evidence, and is not belief against it
entries.summary: Faith in the Bible is the assurance of what God has promised, grounded on what he has shown. He showed himself alive "by many infallible proofs", and has given assurance unto all men in that he raised Jesus from the dead. Believers are bidden to prove all things, to search the Scriptures as the Bereans did, and to give a reason for their hope. The Gospels were written that their readers might believe, and Paul staked the faith on a fact that could be shown false: if Christ be not raised, your faith is vain.

points.claim: Faith is the assurance of things hoped for, and comes by hearing the word of God.
God gave proof: Jesus showed himself alive by many infallible proofs, and his resurrection is God's assurance to all men.
Believers are bidden to test what they hear, and to give a reason for their hope.
The records were written from what was seen, that their readers might believe.
Paul staked the faith on a fact that could be shown false: if Christ is not raised, faith is vain.

objections.objection: Faith is believing without evidence; Jesus blessed those who have not seen.
objections.answer: Those who have not seen believe on the word of those who did, as we believe most of history; John adds at once that these things are written that ye might believe.

objections.objection: If God existed he would make himself plain.
objections.answer: He has spoken by the prophets and by his Son, and raised him before chosen witnesses. Signs did not compel those who would not believe: "neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead." He is not far from any who seek him.

objections.objection: Belief is a matter of upbringing: born elsewhere, you would believe otherwise.
objections.answer: Where a belief came from does not settle whether it is true, and the argument cuts against unbelief as much as belief. The Bereans were commended for searching the Scriptures, not for taking what they were told.

entries.subject: faith
entries.title: Miracles are not incredible if there is a God
entries.summary: A miracle is not an effect without a cause, but an act of the God who made the world and set its ordinances. The Bible's miracles are few, gathered at chosen times, and given as signs with a purpose. They were done openly, and the enemies of Jesus and the apostles granted the works while disputing their source. The witnesses expected none and doubted until they saw. Whether God raised Jesus is a question of evidence, not of what usually happens: "Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?"

points.claim: The God who made the world and set its ordinances can act in it; nothing is too hard for him.

sources.quote: In a word, once believe that there is a God, and miracles are not incredible.

points.claim: The miracles were signs with a purpose, done openly, few and at chosen times.
Enemies granted the works, and disputed only their source.
The witnesses expected no miracle; they doubted until they saw.

objections.objection: Dead men do not rise.
objections.answer: The disciples knew that as well as anyone, and called the women's report idle tales. The claim is not that nature raises the dead, but that God raised Jesus; whether he did is a question of evidence.

objections.objection: Miracles break the laws of nature.
objections.answer: The laws of nature describe what happens when nothing else acts; a hand that catches a falling stone breaks no law. The God who set the ordinances of heaven and earth is not bound by them.

objections.objection: Every religion claims miracles.
objections.answer: Claims are tested, not counted: Elijah put the gods to a public test, and a prophet whose word failed was not to be feared. Scripture itself warns of false signs. The resurrection rests on named witnesses, a known tomb, and a movement begun in the city where it happened.

entries.subject: morality
entries.title: Right and wrong are real, and point to a Lawgiver
entries.summary: Men everywhere know that some things are truly wrong, not merely disliked: Paul says the work of the law is written in their hearts, their conscience bearing witness. Man is made in the image of God, so his life has a worth no one else gave and no one may take. If there is no Lawgiver, good and evil are only preference and custom, and a people that called evil good would be different, not wrong. The prophets condemn exactly that, and God requires of man to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with him.

points.claim: Men everywhere know right and wrong: the work of the law is written in their hearts.
Man is made in the image of God, and so has a worth no one else gave him.
Without a Lawgiver, every man does what is right in his own eyes; the prophets condemn calling evil good.
God requires justice, mercy and humility, and sums the law in love of God and neighbour.

objections.objection: Atheists can be good without God.
objections.answer: They can, and Paul says why: the law is written in their hearts. The question is not whether a man can do good without believing in God, but why good binds him at all.

objections.objection: Morality evolved, or is what a society agrees.
objections.answer: Then a society that agreed to cruelty would not be wrong, only different. Yet we judge whole nations, and honour those who stood against their own; to do so is to appeal to a standard above every people.

objections.objection: Religion has done great evil.
objections.answer: Much has been done in Christ's name that he forbade. He told Peter to put up his sword, said his kingdom was not of this world, and foretold that wolves would arise among his followers. Judge the teaching by its teacher, not by those who departed from it.

entries.subject: morality
entries.title: Deuteronomy 20:16-18, the destruction of the Canaanites, read as genocide
entries.summary: The command was a judgement on nations whose iniquity God had borne for four hundred years, who burned their sons and daughters to their gods. It was not for race or for Israel's righteousness: the same land would spue out Israel for the same sins, and did. It was for that land at that time, not a standing command, and those who turned, as Rahab and the Gibeonites, were spared. The Judge of all the earth does right, and has no pleasure in the death of the wicked.

points.claim: God waited four hundred years, until the Amorites' iniquity was full.
Their sins are named, among them the burning of their children; it was for their wickedness, not Israel's righteousness.
It was not for race: Israel was warned the land would spue them out for the same sins, and it did.
Those who turned were spared: Rahab and her house, and the Gibeonites.
The Judge of all the earth does right, and has no pleasure in the death of the wicked.

objections.objection: Even the children were killed.
objections.answer: They were, as in the flood and in Sodom, and as every child of Adam dies under God's hand. He who gives life has the right to take it; and Abraham, pleading for Sodom, found that the Judge would spare the whole city for ten righteous.

objections.objection: Every conquest has been justified by a god's command.
objections.answer: This was given once, for one land, its end foretold four centuries before by a prophet whose word was proved. No one now has such a command, and Christ forbade his disciples the sword.

entries.subject: morality
entries.title: Exodus 21:2-11, the law of servants, read as the Bible approving slavery
entries.summary: The law did not invent bondage but restrained it. Stealing and selling a man was death; a Hebrew who sold himself for debt went free in the seventh year, with provision, and was not to be ruled with rigour; a servant maimed by his master went free; and a runaway was not to be handed back. Some of its allowances, as with divorce, were given for the hardness of men's hearts. The gospel made master and servant brothers under one Master, bade the servant take his freedom if he could, and condemned menstealers.

points.claim: Stealing and selling a man was punished with death.
A Hebrew who sold himself for debt went free in the seventh year, with provision, and was not to be ruled with rigour.
A servant maimed by his master went free, and his death was avenged.
A runaway servant was not to be handed back to his master.
In Christ master and servant are brothers under one Master, and the servant may take his freedom.

objections.objection: Leviticus 25:44-46 lets Israel keep servants of other nations for ever.
objections.answer: It did, and that is not to be explained away. The law regulated a hard world it did not yet end, as Jesus said of divorce: because of the hardness of your hearts. Yet those servants too were freed if maimed, avenged if killed, and not handed back if they fled.

objections.objection: Paul told servants to obey their masters, and sent Onesimus back.
objections.answer: He told masters to forbear threatening, knowing their own Master is in heaven, and servants to take freedom if they could. He sent Onesimus back not as a servant but a brother beloved, to be received as Paul himself.

entries.subject: resurrection
entries.title: The tomb was empty
entries.summary: Jesus was buried in a known tomb belonging to a member of the council, and within weeks the apostles were preaching his resurrection in the same city. His enemies never produced the body; they said instead that the disciples had stolen it, which grants that the tomb was empty. The first witnesses were women, whose testimony counted for little then: no one inventing the story would have chosen them.

points.claim: The tomb was known: Joseph of Arimathea, a counsellor, laid Jesus in his own tomb, and the women saw where he was laid.
The resurrection was preached in Jerusalem, where the body could have been produced to end it.
The rulers paid the guard to say the disciples stole the body: they did not deny it was gone.
Women were the first witnesses, an embarrassing detail no inventor would choose; even the apostles thought their words idle tales.
The grave clothes lay in order, the napkin folded apart: not the work of thieves.

objections.objection: The disciples stole the body.
objections.answer: The tomb was sealed and guarded at the rulers' request, and the disciples had fled. Men who knew the story false would not have suffered and died for it.

objections.objection: The women went to the wrong tomb.
objections.answer: They had watched him laid there two days before, and Joseph, its owner, knew it. The rulers had only to go to the right one.

objections.objection: Jesus only fainted on the cross and revived.
objections.answer: The soldiers, whose trade was execution, found him dead and did not break his legs; the spear brought blood and water; Pilate had the centurion confirm the death. A half-dead man could not have persuaded anyone he had conquered death.

entries.subject: resurrection
entries.title: He was seen alive by many witnesses
entries.summary: Paul lists those who saw Jesus alive: Peter, the twelve, over five hundred at once, most still living when he wrote and able to be asked, James, and Paul himself. He was seen by groups and by individuals, indoors and out, over forty days; he was touched and he ate. Hallucinations are private and do not happen to five hundred at once.

points.claim: Paul names witnesses, and says most of the five hundred were still alive: an invitation to check.
He showed them his hands and feet, was handled, and ate before them.
He was seen over forty days, by groups and individuals, in Jerusalem and Galilee.

objections.objection: They saw visions or hallucinations.
objections.answer: Hallucinations are private, come to those expecting them, and do not eat. The disciples did not expect him and did not at first believe; groups saw him together; and the appearances stopped after forty days.

entries.subject: resurrection
entries.title: The witnesses were changed and suffered for it
entries.summary: At his arrest the disciples fled and Peter denied him; weeks later they stood before the council that had killed him and would not stop speaking. James his brother had not believed him; he became a leader of the ecclesia in Jerusalem and was stoned for it. Paul persecuted the ecclesia until he saw Jesus. Men may die for a lie they believe, but not for one they made up.

points.claim: The disciples fled and Peter denied him; afterwards they defied the council.
James, who did not believe in him, saw him risen and led the ecclesia in Jerusalem. Josephus records his stoning.
Paul, the persecutor, was turned by seeing him, and gave up everything for it.

objections.objection: People of every faith have died for what they believe.
objections.answer: They died for what they had been taught. The apostles died for what they said they had seen and handled, and would have known if it were false.

entries.subject: resurrection
entries.title: Jesus died on the cross
entries.summary: That Jesus was crucified under Pontius Pilate is among the best attested facts of ancient history. All four Gospels and Paul's earliest letters record it; Tacitus writes that Christus suffered the extreme penalty under Pilate; and the first preaching, in Jerusalem itself, was of a crucified Messiah, a scandal no one would invent. Soldiers whose trade was execution confirmed his death. The prophets foretold that the Messiah would be cut off and pierced, and Jesus foretold it himself.

points.claim: The Gospels, Acts and Paul all record his crucifixion and death.
A crucified Messiah was a stumbling block to Jews and folly to Greeks: no one would invent it.
Roman soldiers confirmed his death, and Pilate asked the centurion before giving up the body.
Tacitus records that Christus suffered the extreme penalty under Pontius Pilate, in the reign of Tiberius.
The prophets and Jesus foretold that the Messiah would be cut off and killed.

objections.objection: He was not killed or crucified, but it was made to appear so (Qur'an 4:157).
objections.answer: That was written six centuries later and far from Judaea, against witnesses who were there, enemies as well as friends. Jesus said he must be killed and rise the third day, and his disciples suffered for saying he did. The Qur'an itself has Jesus speak of the day he dies and the day he is raised alive (19:33).

objections.objection: He fainted on the cross and revived in the tomb.
objections.answer: Soldiers whose trade was execution found him dead, and a spear brought out blood and water. A man half dead from scourging and the cross, freeing himself from the tomb, would not have persuaded his disciples that he had conquered death.

entries.subject: records
entries.title: The records are early and from eyewitnesses
entries.summary: Paul passes on a summary of the gospel he had received, naming witnesses of the resurrection; he wrote about AD 55 and had met Peter and James within a few years of the crucifixion. Acts ends with Paul alive in Rome, before his death and the fall of Jerusalem, and Luke's Gospel came before it. Roman and Jewish writers confirm that Jesus was put to death under Pilate and that his followers spread from Judaea.

points.claim: Paul delivered what he had received, and met Peter and James three years after his conversion.
Luke wrote from eyewitnesses with care, and Acts, his second volume, ends before Paul's death.
The apostles claimed to be eyewitnesses, and appealed to things done openly.

Tacitus records that Christus was executed by Pontius Pilate under Tiberius; Josephus mentions James "the brother of Jesus, who was called Christ"; Pliny describes Christians singing to Christ as to a god. Josephus' longer passage on Jesus (18.63-64) has been added to by Christian copyists and is not relied on here.

objections.objection: The Gospels were written generations later, after legends grew.
objections.answer: Acts says nothing of Paul's death, Nero's persecution or Jerusalem's fall, though all bear on its story; it was written before them, and Luke before Acts. Paul's summary of the witnesses is earlier still.

entries.subject: records
entries.title: Jesus lived, and was put to death under Pontius Pilate
entries.summary: The Gospels set Jesus among named rulers, places and years. Paul, writing within twenty-five years, had met his brother James and his disciple Peter. Tacitus records that Christus suffered under Pontius Pilate, and Josephus names James "the brother of Jesus, who was called Christ". His enemies called him a deceiver and said his body was stolen; none said he never lived. That he lived and was crucified is granted by historians of every belief.

points.claim: The Gospels set him among named rulers, places and years.
Paul met Peter and James the Lord's brother three years after his conversion, and wrote within twenty-five years of the crucifixion.
Tacitus records that Christus suffered under Pontius Pilate; Josephus names James, the brother of Jesus who was called Christ.
His enemies called him a deceiver and said his body was stolen; none said he never lived.

objections.objection: Jesus is a myth, copied from pagan gods who died and rose.
objections.answer: The first believers were Jews who had turned from idols and loathed the gods of the nations. They preached a man crucified under a known governor and raised on the third day before named witnesses, not a god of the seasons dying every year. The resurrection they hoped for was Israel's, of the dead at the last day; his came first.

objections.objection: No record from his own lifetime names him.
objections.answer: Few records of anyone from first-century Galilee survive, and a carpenter's son put to death as a criminal would not be written in Rome's annals while he lived. Paul's letters are within a generation, and Tacitus and Josephus within a lifetime.

entries.subject: records
entries.title: The Gospels differ as independent witnesses do, and agree in substance
entries.summary: Four accounts agree in substance and differ in detail, as honest witnesses do; agreement in every word would point to collusion. One account often explains another without meaning to: John says Jesus asked Philip where to buy bread, and only Luke says they were near Bethsaida, and only John that Philip came from there. Most differences are of selection: one names the angel who spoke, another the two who were there. They kept what told against themselves: the disciples' unbelief and Peter's denial.

points.claim: The accounts agree in substance and differ in detail, as independent witnesses do.

sources.quote: There is enough of discrepancy to show that there could have been no previous concert among them; and at the same time such substantial agreement as to show that they all were independent narrators of the same great transaction, as the events actually occurred.

points.claim: One account explains another without meaning to: Philip is asked about bread near Bethsaida, his own city; the green grass of Mark is the spring of John's Passover.
Differences are of selection, not contradiction: one names the angel who spoke, another the two who were there.
They kept what told against them: the disciples' unbelief and Peter's denial.

objections.objection: The resurrection accounts contradict each other on the women, the angels and the hour.
objections.answer: To name one woman or one angel is not to deny the others: John names only Mary Magdalene, yet she says "we know not where they have laid him." They set out while it was yet dark and came at the rising of the sun.

objections.objection: Matthew says Judas hanged himself; Acts says he fell headlong and burst asunder.
objections.answer: Both can be true of one death: he hanged himself, and his body fell. The priests bought the field with his money, so Acts reckons it his.

entries.subject: prophecy
entries.title: The Bible foretold what came to pass
entries.summary: Moses foretold that Israel would be scattered among all nations, and the prophets that they would not be made an end of but gathered again to their land: they were scattered by Babylon and by Rome, kept distinct for two thousand years, and are a nation in the land again. Daniel named the kingdoms that would follow Babylon. The prophets foretold where the Messiah would be born, that he would be rejected, pierced and bear the sins of many. Jesus foretold that Jerusalem would be compassed with armies and its temple thrown down within that generation, and Rome did it in AD 70.

points.claim: Israel would be scattered among all nations, yet not made an end of, and gathered again.
Daniel named the kingdoms to follow Babylon: the Medes and Persians, then Grecia.
The Messiah's birthplace, rejection, death among transgressors and burial with the rich were foretold.
Jesus foretold Jerusalem's siege and the temple's overthrow within that generation.

objections.objection: The prophecies were written after the events.
objections.answer: The Jews who rejected Jesus kept the same prophets, translated into Greek before his birth, and could not have written them to fit him. Israel's scattering, preservation and return run to the present day, long after any date proposed for the books.

objections.objection: Daniel was written in the second century BC, after the events it describes.
objections.answer: Jesus called Daniel a prophet. And the fourth kingdom, iron, which breaks in pieces and is divided, is Rome, which rose after any date proposed for the book.

entries.subject: prophecy
entries.title: The Messiah was to come before the second temple fell
entries.summary: Jacob foretold that the sceptre would not depart from Judah until Shiloh came. Daniel foretold that Messiah the Prince would be cut off, and after that the city and the sanctuary destroyed. Haggai and Malachi said the Lord would come to the second temple, and its glory would be greater than the first's. That temple fell in AD 70: if the Messiah was to come while it stood, he has come, and Jesus is the one who taught in it and foretold its fall.

points.claim: The sceptre would not depart from Judah until Shiloh came.
Messiah the Prince would be cut off, and then the city and the sanctuary destroyed.
The Lord would suddenly come to his temple, the second, and fill it with greater glory than the first.
Jesus came to that temple, taught in it, and foretold its overthrow, which came in AD 70.

objections.objection: Daniel's weeks cannot be counted exactly.
objections.answer: Their starting point is disputed, and this entry does not rest on a count of days. However they are counted, the Messiah is cut off before the city and sanctuary are destroyed, and they were destroyed in AD 70.

entries.subject: prophecy
entries.title: Isaiah 52:13-53:12, the suffering servant, read as the nation of Israel
entries.summary: Israel is called the servant elsewhere, but this servant is stricken "for the transgression of my people", so he is not the people. He had done no violence, neither was any deceit in his mouth, which the prophets never say of the nation. He is cut off out of the land of the living, makes his grave with the wicked and with the rich, and after his death prolongs his days and sees his seed. The Targum on the Prophets names him the Messiah. Jesus fulfils each line.

points.claim: He is stricken for the transgression of "my people", and so is distinct from them.
He is without violence or deceit, as the prophets do not say Israel was.
He dies, is buried, and lives again to see his seed.
Jesus was rejected, silent before his accusers, numbered with transgressors and buried by a rich man.
The Targum on the Prophets names the servant the Messiah, though it turns his sufferings onto Israel's enemies.

objections.objection: Isaiah calls Israel the servant (41:8; 49:3).
objections.answer: And the servant of chapter 49 is sent to bring Jacob again to God and raise up the tribes of Israel, so he is not Israel itself; he bears Israel's name as its true representative, as Jesus was called out of Egypt as Israel was.

entries.subject: scripture
entries.title: The Bible has been kept, not corrupted
entries.summary: The Dead Sea Scrolls, copied before Christ, give the Old Testament in the words read today, with differences of spelling and small slips. The New Testament survives in more and earlier manuscripts than any other ancient book, so a change in one would be shown up by the rest. Jesus said his words would not pass away, and the Qur'an itself bids the people of the Gospel judge by it, and Muhammad, if in doubt, ask those who read the Book before him: if the Bible was corrupted, it was not corrupted after that.

points.claim: God's word endures, and Jesus said his words would not pass away.
The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran, copied a century or more before Christ, agrees with the Isaiah read today in all but small details.

The New Testament is known from thousands of Greek manuscripts, some within a few generations of the writers, and from early translations and quotations; their differences are mostly of spelling and order, and none changes the gospel.
The Qur'an bids the people of the Gospel judge by what God revealed in it, and Muhammad, if in doubt, ask those who read the Book before him.

objections.objection: The Gospels were changed after Jesus' time.
objections.answer: Then they were changed before the manuscripts we have, everywhere at once, among churches scattered and divided, without a trace. Peter already counted Paul's letters with the other Scriptures.

entries.subject: scripture
entries.title: Scripture is complete, and tests every later word
entries.summary: All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works. The faith was once delivered unto the saints. Paul said that even an angel from heaven preaching another gospel is accursed, and Isaiah: "To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them." Later books, prophets and teachers are tested by the Scriptures already given, as the Bereans tested Paul.

points.claim: Scripture is inspired, and makes the believer complete.
The faith was delivered once; another gospel, even from an angel, is accursed.
Every teacher is tested by the word already given.

objections.objection: God has spoken again since, by a later prophet or book.
objections.answer: A later prophet must agree with the earlier: Moses said one who leads after other gods is false even if his sign comes to pass. A book that denies that Jesus died and rose, or that adds gods, fails that test.

objections.objection: Jesus promised that the spirit would guide into all truth, still to come.
objections.answer: He promised it to the apostles, who were to be his witnesses, and they wrote what it taught them.

entries.subject: scripture
entries.title: Tradition does not stand beside Scripture
entries.summary: Jesus rebuked those who made the word of God of none effect by their tradition, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men. The apostles delivered traditions, by word and by letter, but what they delivered is written; later councils and customs are tested by it, not added to it. Many traditions arose long after them: prayers to the dead, images in worship, a priesthood forbidden to marry, the baptism of infants. A teaching that cannot be shown from the apostles' writings did not come from the apostles.

points.claim: Jesus set the commandment of God against the tradition of men.
Paul warned against the tradition of men, and against those forbidding to marry.
What the apostles delivered they wrote, that we may know it, and not think above what is written.

objections.objection: Paul says to hold the traditions taught "whether by word, or our epistle".
objections.answer: He means what he himself taught the Thessalonians, in person or by letter. It does not reach to teachings first known centuries later: the test of whether a teaching came from Paul is whether Paul wrote it.

objections.objection: The church gave us the Bible, so its authority is above it.
objections.answer: The ecclesia recognised the Scriptures; it did not make them. Israel was entrusted with the oracles of God, and Jesus still judged its tradition by them.

entries.subject: scripture
entries.title: Matthew 16:18, "upon this rock I will build my church", read as Peter and the popes
entries.summary: The rock is the truth Peter had just confessed, "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God": Scripture calls God and Christ the rock, and the foundation no man can lay other than Jesus Christ. Peter is a stone built on it, as he wrote that every believer is a living stone. He used the keys he was given, opening the gospel to Jews at Pentecost and to Gentiles at Caesarea, and the same binding and loosing was given to all the disciples. Paul withstood him, James gave judgement at Jerusalem, and nothing passes his place to a successor.

points.claim: The rock is Christ, whom Peter confessed.
The apostles together are the foundation, and binding and loosing was given to all.
Peter used the keys, opening the door to Jews and to Gentiles.
Peter was not over the others: Paul withstood him, James gave the judgement, and Peter called himself a fellow elder.

objections.objection: Peter's name means rock.
objections.answer: It does, and he was a stone built on the rock, as he wrote: "Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house."

entries.subject: scripture
entries.title: The Apocrypha is not Scripture
entries.summary: The books Catholics and Orthodox add to the Old Testament, Tobit, Judith, the Maccabees and the rest, were never received by the Jews, to whom "were committed the oracles of God". Jesus named the Scriptures as the law of Moses, the prophets and the psalms, and neither he nor the apostles ever cite these books as Scripture. They do not claim to be prophecy: the first book of Maccabees says the prophets had ceased in its day, and the second closes by asking pardon if it was written poorly. Purgatory and prayer for the dead rest on them, not on the Scriptures Jesus received.

points.claim: The oracles of God were committed to the Jews, and they never received these books.
Jesus named the Scriptures in their three parts: the law of Moses, the prophets and the psalms.
Christ and the apostles quote the law, the prophets and the psalms as Scripture again and again, and these books never.

The books disclaim prophecy: 1 Maccabees says the prophets had ceased in its day, and 2 Maccabees ends by asking pardon if it was written poorly. Scripture is given by the spirit, not by the writer's skill.

objections.objection: The early church read them, and they were in the Greek Old Testament.
objections.answer: They were read, as many books were, but being read beside Scripture does not make a book Scripture; Jerome, who translated the Latin Bible, set them apart from the canon. The test is the oracles committed to the Jews, which Jesus received.

objections.objection: Jude quotes the book of Enoch, so the apostles used books outside the canon.
objections.answer: Jude cites a saying, as Paul cites Greek poets, without calling the book Scripture. None of the apostles introduces these books with "it is written" or "the Scripture saith".

entries.subject: scripture
entries.title: No later prophet or book adds to Scripture
entries.summary: The faith was "once delivered unto the saints", and Paul wrote: "though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed." Every later voice claiming to add to it, the Book of Mormon, Ellen White's visions, the Watchtower's "faithful and discreet slave", the Qur'an, Bahá'u'lláh, the inner light, Mary Baker Eddy's Science and Health, is tested by the word already given: "if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them." Each teaches what the apostles did not, and several foretold what did not come to pass.

points.claim: The faith was delivered once, complete, and another gospel is accursed, even from an angel.
Every prophet is tried by the word already given, and the spirits are to be tested.
A prophet whose word does not come to pass has not spoken from Yahweh.
Christ warned of false prophets, and of those who would say he had come again in secret.
Nothing is to be added to the prophecy of the book.

objections.objection: God has always sent prophets; why would he stop?
objections.answer: He has spoken in these last days by his Son, and the spirit was given to the apostles to guide them into all truth. The next voice Scripture promises is Christ's own at his coming, not another book before it.

objections.objection: The light within, or the spirit, guides me beyond the letter.
objections.answer: The spirit that gave the Scriptures does not contradict them, and the heart unchecked by the word deceives: "The heart is deceitful above all things." The Bereans were commended for searching the Scriptures, even of what an apostle preached.

entries.subject: scripture
entries.title: Deuteronomy 18:18, "a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee", read as Muhammad
entries.summary: Moses spoke to Israel: "Yahweh thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren." In the same book "thy brethren" are the tribes of Israel, from whom the king must also come and not a stranger. Peter and Stephen preached that the prophet was Jesus, an Israelite of Judah, and the crowds that saw his signs said, "This is of a truth that prophet." Like Moses he spoke with God face to face, did signs and wonders, was rejected by his own, and mediated a covenant.

points.claim: The prophet is raised "from the midst of thee, of thy brethren": from Israel, as the king must be.
Peter and Stephen preached that Moses' prophet is Jesus.
Those who saw his signs knew him as the prophet who should come.
No prophet arose like Moses, whom Yahweh knew face to face, in signs and wonders, until Christ, who spoke the Father's words and worked his works.

objections.objection: The brethren of Israel are the Ishmaelites, the sons of Abraham's other son.
objections.answer: In Deuteronomy "brethren" are the tribes, and the Levites have no inheritance "among their brethren", the other tribes. Edom is once called a brother, but the prophet is raised "from the midst of thee".

objections.objection: Jesus was not like Moses: he brought no law and led no nation.
